questions.q: What does the Lookup transformation do?
options: Joins data flow input columns with columns in a reference dataset, row by row inside the pipeline
Sorts the data flow into ascending or descending order
Splits a data flow into multiple outputs based on conditions
Converts a column's data type to a different data type
questions.explain: The Lookup transformation performs an equi-join between input columns and a reference dataset — a table, view, query result, or cache file — to pull in related values.

questions.q: Which Lookup cache mode loads the entire reference dataset into memory once, before the transformation runs?
options: Full cache
Partial cache
No cache
Live cache
questions.explain: Full cache queries the reference dataset once during the pre-execute phase and holds it entirely in memory for the rest of execution — fast, but a single point-in-time snapshot.

questions.q: By default, what happens to a Lookup row that finds no matching entry in the reference dataset?
options: It's treated as an error, unless you configure the Lookup to redirect it to a no match output instead
It's silently dropped from the data flow
It's automatically sent to the Match output with null values
The package throws a compile-time error before it can even run
questions.explain: Unmatched rows are handled as errors by default. You have to explicitly select 'Redirect rows to no match output' on the General page to route them to the No Match output instead.

questions.q: Why does source data with inconsistent casing (like 'Smith' vs. 'SMITH') sometimes cause Lookup transformation failures?
options: Lookup comparisons are case sensitive
The Lookup transformation only supports uppercase strings
SSIS automatically lowercases all string columns before a Lookup
Case sensitivity only affects the Merge Join transformation, not Lookup
questions.explain: Lookups performed by the Lookup transformation are case sensitive. The fix is to normalize case first — with a Character Map transformation, or UPPER/LOWER in the reference query.

questions.q: If the reference dataset has multiple rows that match a given input row, what does the Lookup transformation do?
options: It returns only the first match and does not duplicate the input row
It duplicates the input row once for every match found
It automatically fails the package
It averages the values from every matching row
questions.explain: The Lookup transformation returns only the first match returned by the lookup query — it does not fan out the input row for multiple matches.
